To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the gene expression profile in the mammary gland is altered by dietary fat, and that these changes are associated with the development of mammary tumours in the rat.
diets high in corn oil and extra virgin olive oil differentially modified the gene expression profiles of mammary gland tissues and influenced experimental breast cancer susceptibility.

(i) diets rich in extra virgin olive oil and corn oil differentially affect the gene expression profile in the mammary gland; (ii) diets rich in corn oil and extra virgin olive oil differentially influence the development and progression of mammary tumors in rats and (iii) the dietary fatty acids, linoleic acid (LA), oleic acid (OA), and alpha-linolenic acid (ALA) have differential effects on mammary gland and breast tumor development.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of dietary fat and its effect on mammary gland development, and its relationship with breast cancer susceptibility.
the effect of different dietary fats on mammary gland gene expression and the relationship between gene expression and breast cancer.
the role of diet on mammary gland development and breast cancer susceptibility.

the use of olive oil is a healthy choice for the heart, brain and other parts of the body.
the consumption of extra-virgin oil may be a beneficial strategy to reduce the risk of breast cancer.
a diet high in extra-virgen olive oil is associated with a reduced risk of breast cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have identified a gene expression profile in the mammary gland that is differentially regulated by corn oil and olive oil and that this gene expression profile is associated with experimental breast cancer risk.
the expression profiles of the mammary glands of rats on a corn oil or extra virgin olive oil diet were significantly different.

the expression of a large number of genes in the mammary gland is differentially modified by corn oil (CO) or extra-virgen olive oil (EVOO) and that these modifications are associated with the differential susceptibility to mammary cancer in response to these two dietary fats.

a diet rich in olive oil is a healthy choice for breast cancer survivors.
the diet can influence breast cancer risk.
the type of fat you eat can influence the risk of breast cancer.
